Core Web Vitals: Complete guide for user experience optimization and SEO performance improvement

What are Core Web Vitals?

Core Web Vitals are a set of performance indicators established by Google to objectively evaluate the real user experience on a web page. Officially introduced in 2020, these values are part of the "Web Vitals" initiative, which aims to help website owners measure and improve the experience offered to visitors. Unlike traditional metrics, such as server response speed or total loading time, Core Web Vitals focus on what the user actually feels when interacting with a page. That's why Google decided to include these values as an official ranking factor in search algorithms.

What are the three essential Core Web Vitals values?

Each Core Web Vital measures a distinct aspect of page experience. Google monitors the following three components:

1. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): loading performance

LCP measures the time needed for the largest visible element in the visible area of the page (above the fold) to load completely. Most of the time, this element is an image or a large block of text. A good LCP means the page displays quickly and allows the user to interact without delays.

  • Google benchmark: Under 2.5 seconds is considered optimal.

2. First Input Delay (FID): Interactivity

FID measures the time between the user's first interaction with the page (for example, a click on a link or button) and the moment when the browser actually responds to that interaction. This indicator is essential for interactive websites and web applications.

  • Google benchmark: Under 100 milliseconds provides a good experience.

3. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): visual stability

CLS quantifies how much visual elements move on a page during loading. If texts, images, or buttons move unexpectedly, the user might accidentally click on the wrong element, affecting the overall experience.

  • Google benchmark: Under 0.1 is ideal for stability.

Why do Core Web Vitals matter for SEO?

Google has integrated Core Web Vitals into its ranking algorithm, recognizing the importance of user experience as a relevance factor. Websites that offer superior performance in these three areas can benefit from:

  • Better rankings in organic search results.
  • Decreased bounce rate.
  • Increased session duration on website.
  • A higher conversion rate (leads, sales, subscriptions, etc.).

In a competitive environment, a website optimized for Core Web Vitals has a clear advantage over competitors who don't prioritize these aspects.

Comparison between websites: Google's evaluation

Google doesn't analyze values in isolation. Instead, it compares your page's performance with values from other similar websites targeting the same keywords. This competitive approach means that to achieve higher positions, it's not enough to be "good": you need to be "better than others".

How can you measure Core Web Vitals?

There are several free and accurate tools offered by Google and third parties, through which you can analyze performance in detail:

  • Google PageSpeed Insights: provides scores and detailed recommendations for each Vital.
  • Google Search Console: the "Core Web Vitals" section displays real data from users.
  • Lighthouse: a tool from Chrome DevTools for technical audits.
  • Chrome UX Report: aggregated dataset from real browser usage.

Strategies for improving LCP (loading time)

  • Optimize images using modern formats (WebP, AVIF).
  • Remove blocking caused by unnecessary JavaScript and CSS.
  • Use lazy loading for media elements.
  • Minimize HTTP requests and use efficient caches.

Strategies for reducing FID (interaction delay)

  • Defer execution of non-essential JavaScript.
  • Use Web Workers to handle complex tasks.
  • Remove third-party plugins or scripts that affect response time.

Strategies for reducing CLS (visual stability)

  • Reserve space for images, ads, or iframes through fixed dimensions.
  • Avoid inserting dynamic content at the top of the page after loading.
  • Ensure font loading order to avoid "flash of unstyled text".

Impact of Core Web Vitals on conversions

Studies show that improving website technical performance has direct effects on conversions. For example:

  • Walmart observed a 2% increase in conversion rate for every second reduced in loading time.
  • BBC reported losing 10% of users for every additional second of delay.

Therefore, Core Web Vitals optimization is not just an SEO requirement, but a clear investment in the overall performance of your online business.

The future: what comes after Core Web Vitals?

Google has announced expanding the concept through the "Interaction to Next Paint" (INP) initiative, which will replace FID as the main interactivity metric. This will measure the total time until the page visually reacts to user actions. The update is scheduled for official launch in 2024, which means that continuous optimization will become a permanent part of technical SEO strategy.

Final recommendations

  • Periodically audit website performance using Google PageSpeed Insights.
  • Prioritize changes that impact LCP, FID, and CLS.
  • Work in teams with web developers and SEO specialists to integrate good practices in every page update.

Core Web Vitals are more than simple technical values. They reflect how visitors perceive the experience on your website: and this perception directly influences Google results, conversion rate and user loyalty. In a constantly changing digital landscape, optimizing these metrics is essential for the success of any online project.
